bets.verdict: The slips are settled and the kettle’s on, so here’s your report from the Gaffer — no spin, no hiding, just what happened. A blank, and it stings — nothing landed, the ledger takes a knock, and I take it on the chin in public, because that’s the deal we have. Everything stood up except Montreal Impact v Toronto, which froze at 0-0 — that’s the one I’d want back, and the one I’ll be studying over breakfast. Whatever yesterday gave us, today asks a new question — and I’ll have an answer on the board by breakfast, same as always.

Team talk time — the whistle’s gone on everything we backed, so let’s tot up the damage and the glory in that order or the other. Winner. Not a dramatic one, not a lucky one — just the form doing what the form’s been doing for weeks, with our money sat on top of it. Sweetest of the winners was Zhejiang FC v Qingdao Jonoon — neither defence turned up, which is precisely why we were there, and the 3-2 paid us in full. We log it, we learn from it, and we go again — the beautiful thing about this game is there’s always another card tomorrow, and I intend to read it better than the bookies do.

I’ve had my coffee and read the scores twice, so here it is — yesterday’s verdict, straight from the man who picked them. I’ll not dress it up: both slips went down, and no amount of clever words turns red into green. It happens to every honest record — the dishonest ones just delete days like this. The dud was the both-teams-to-score in Djurgården v Halmstad — Halmstad couldn’t buy a goal at 3-0, and one shy front line is all it takes to sink that market. Long game, this — one day never makes us and one day never breaks us, which is exactly why the record stays public and the method stays the same.

Right, pull up a chair, because I owe you the honest word on yesterday’s slips — the good, the bad, and the bits I’d rather not talk about. Rough day at the office — both bets lost, and while the reads were right more than the results suggest, results are what pay, so we log it and move. Blame the corners in Akureyri v Akranes — two wide-loving teams picked yesterday to play through the middle, and our line never got close. Right, that’s the accounting done — now if you’ll excuse me, tomorrow’s form tables aren’t going to squint at themselves.

Every morning I mark my own homework in public, which is either brave or daft depending on the scoreline — let’s find out which today. Mixed bag, and I’ll give it to you straight: the double banked, the treble came up a leg short, and the ledger still moved the right direction — which is the bit that matters. The pick of the winners was the Harju Jalgpallikool game — 3-0, 3 goals for the greedy, and the sweet feeling of watching a form read play out to the letter. The card never sleeps and neither does the spreadsheet — see you in the morning with the next round of value.
